title: Deployment Extensions: Part 1
gist: A Sailor Pulse podcast episode note flags that U.S. Navy carrier deployments are running the longest since Vietnam, straining ships and crews, and frames the Optimized Fleet Response Plan's failure plus combatant-commander-versus-service tug-of-war as the drivers of repeated deployment extensions.

insights.claim: U.S. Navy carrier deployments are running at record lengths since Vietnam and the resulting extensions are the issue currently defining fleet life for sailors.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Sustained over-deployment accelerates hull and airframe wear, pulling forward maintenance, repair and shipbuilding demand for naval primes.
insights.quote: record-setting cruises since Vietnam are straining ships and crews

insights.claim: The Optimized Fleet Response Plan, designed to make Navy deployment cycles predictable, has not fixed the extension problem it was meant to solve.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Failure of the readiness-cycle framework signals persistent structural undersupply of deployable hulls relative to demand.
insights.quote: They trace what the Optimized Fleet Response Plan was meant to fix

insights.claim: A structural tug-of-war between combatant commanders demanding forces and the services trying to preserve them determines who deploys and for how long.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for reading force-posture news: demand-side commanders consistently win over supply-side services, implying continued high operational tempo.
insights.quote: the tug-of-war between combatant commanders and the services shapes who deploys

insights.claim: Extended deployments are being framed as a retention and personnel issue for sailors caught between competing institutional demands, not merely a scheduling problem.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Personnel attrition is the slow-burn cost of high tempo and a leading indicator of future readiness shortfalls.
insights.quote: the sailors caught in the middle
